findings.claim: The guard in the field/second-member loop is inverted. `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) Add(...)` never adds a string-keyed member that is not already present, so string-keyed members on this path are silently dropped from the collected object info. The generated formatter would then omit them, and serialized output loses data. When the key already exists, the call still throws on the duplicate Add, which is the crash the sibling hunks were trying to prevent.

Serialize an instance with base-built and head-built generated formatters and compare bytes: head's map should be missing A and B. As a cheaper check, assert the head-generated formatter source contains "A" and "B"; it should not.
